title: Product
description: A product: its roles, its open questions, and the kinds and relations it declares as its own. It also holds the command layer, whose commands are written once for every kind: each add, change, move, link, unlink or removal changes the one aggregate of the record it names, and applying several changes or merging two branches changes several, each recorded as an exception.

title: Read model
description: A shape of data a domain reads: its fields, its queries and their handlers, its projection, and the tables that store data, with their keys.

title: Use case
description: A goal someone reaches: its actors, its requirements with their tests, and its flow with its steps and test.

title: View
description: A place in the app where flow steps happen: its requirements with their tests.

title: Endpoint
description: An operation exposed over HTTP: its requirements with their tests, and its handler.

title: Integration
description: Another system a product exchanges with: its adapter and its tests.

title: UI component
description: A piece of the interface that renders views.

title: Pattern
description: Behavior several use cases share, written once: its rules, its settings, the value each follower gives a setting, and each rule's tests per following domain.

title: Standard
description: Engineering rules the product's code follows, with the rules themselves.

title: Domain
description: A business capability of a product: its terms, its capabilities in order, and its domain services with what implements and proves them.

title: Specification
description: A rule that decides whether a record satisfies it, with its predicate and its test.

title: Aggregate
description: A consistency boundary of a domain: its entities and their fields and data models, its repository, and its invariants with their tests.

title: Domain event
description: Something that happened to an aggregate: its fields and the event type that delivers it.

title: Command
description: An intent to change an aggregate: its handler, the other aggregates it records as changing in its transaction, and the policies it runs, with their handlers and tests.

title: Value object
description: A value with no identity of its own: its fields, its constraints with their tests, and the value type that implements it.

title: Check
description: One rule the engine applies, as a row of the `check` table: Lathe's in `lathe/data/check.jsonl`, a product's own in its `data/check.jsonl`. Its query reads the typed tables and returns a row for each problem; the problems of a run are rows of the `problem` table, never stored.

title: Product setting
description: A product's settings that its checks read, one row per product: today the most children of one kind a record should hold.

title: Page
description: One place in the app, identified by its address: the products (`/`), a record at its bare ID (`/<id>`, a product's and a domain's being their overview), a group of the graph's tree (a stage or folder, `/<domain-id>/<stage>/<folder>`, or a record's children of one kind, `/<parent-id>/<kind>`), the checks (`/checks`), the reference (`/format`), a kind's or a check's page in it (`/format/kinds/<kind>`, `/format/checks/<check>`), or Appearance (`/settings/appearance`). Every page shows a view of one loaded workspace.
notes:
A product, domain, record or group page shows its one focus in the views that are open, each a pane: Wiki, Graph and, on a domain, aggregate or entity page, Model. The address names them, as in `?view=wiki,graph`; the views never change the path. Such a page has three columns: the navigation, the main view, and the side bar, which shows the focused record's facts. A format page has the same columns, with one pane and the kind's or check's facts in the side bar.

A record's page reads that data and changes it only through the command layer: its Edit, Add and Remove actions send one write each to the server, and the change is reviewed in git like any other.

title: Space
description: One product as a place to work in, kept apart from every other: the pages that belong to it (its Checks page among them), its icon, its place among the other spaces, and the last page visited in it. Nothing of another product shows inside a space. The current space is always the product of the page in hand.

title: Nav row
description: A row of the nav that folds, a domain, a stage, a kind group or a record with children, and whether the reader has it folded, for the browser session.

title: Tab group
description: The pages open at once, as tabs in a row with one active, as an editor group in VS Code. Today each space has one tab group, shown at the left of the page bar above the panes (on a phone, as the Open pages sheet); later each pane could own one. The group's rules hold whatever owns it.

title: Graph settings
description: How the graph is drawn: its layout, depth, filters, trace mode, Links switch and minimap. One for the reader's browser session, shared by every tab and every page, so moving through the graph never changes it.

title: Product repo
description: The repo `lathe init` sets up, whose config names its data folder.

title: Panel
description: A part of the workbench a person shows, hides and resizes: the nav, the panes of a page and the side bar. Hiding a panel gives its room to the others and loses nothing.

title: Keymap
description: The keyboard commands with their bindings, which every key, the palette, the sheet and every hint read.

title: Appearance
description: The person's themes, the theme chosen and the color mode.

title: Product window
description: A desktop window showing one product folder, with its saved place and the server it loads Lathe from.

title: App server
description: What a window loads Lathe from: `serve()` in the shell's own process, the app's Vite dev server that the shell starts, or the owner's dev server on port 5199, which it only shares. `lathe serve` runs the same `serve()`.

title: Recent folders
description: The folders opened last, latest first, which one list serves every window.

title: Pattern following
description: A domain or use case that follows a pattern, and the value it gives each of the pattern's settings. Which rules each domain owes because of it is worked out (RM04), never stored.
